title: Adaptive retry budgets and stream-window idempotency semantics
creator: Ava Chen
description: Introduce cross-SDK primitives and defaults to support adaptive retry budgets and a clear idempotency grace period for streaming and chunked operations. This ticket defines behavioral defaults, telemetry hooks, and sample code for Python/TypeScript/Go clients so application teams can reliably retry without causing duplicate side effects or uncontrolled retry storms.
background: Current SDK retry guidance is conservative and mostly request-level: exponential backoff presets and idempotency keys for discrete request/response flows. Streaming and large/chunked uploads lack a standard idempotency semantics (when to treat a retry as duplicate vs resume) and we also lack a runtime mechanism to cap retries per-caller or per-operation window. On high-load tenants we've observed retry amplification during transient infra flaps and confusion about how long id keys should be considered authoritative for resumable streams.
goals: Define an adaptive retry-budget concept that limits retries per caller/route over sliding windows
Specify a cross-SDK idempotency grace-window semantics for resumable/streaming operations (default TTL and extend behavior)
Provide telemetry metrics and tagging to inform automatic backoff scaling and sampling for analysis
Deliver idiomatic examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go demonstrating usage and migration guidance
Ship conservative SDK defaults that are safe for existing customers and allow opt-in relaxed behaviors
proposed_solution: Retry budget: introduce a token-bucket-style retry budget per API key + route with configurable capacity (default 5 tokens per minute) and refill rate; SDKs expose a RetryBudget client helper so callers can share budgets across concurrent streams.

Backoff scaling: use telemetry-driven adjustment where SDKs increase base backoff multiplier for callers that consume >70% of budget in a 1m window; provide hooks for Redwood Console to suggest tuned presets.

Stream idempotency TTL (grace window): introduce a default 15-minute id key TTL for streaming/resumable operations. A retry with the same id within TTL is treated as resume if the server supports resume, otherwise dedupe on server-side if possible.

Idempotency hints API: add optional metadata headers/fields: X-RW-Id-Key, X-RW-Stream-Offset, X-RW-Resume-Support to allow graceful resume vs naive retry. SDKs encode these fields and surface helpers to generate stable id keys for multipart uploads and chunked streams.

Cross-language ergonomics: provide Python context manager, TypeScript async iterator wrapper, and Go stream helper that manage id key lifecycle and coordinate budget tokens when automatically retrying chunks.
Telemetry: emit metrics: rw.sdk.retry.attempts, rw.sdk.retry.budget_remaining, rw.sdk.stream.idkey.used, rw.sdk.stream.resume.success; tag with sdk.lang, sdk.version, route, and error_class.
Fallback policy: if budget exhausted, SDK returns a RetryBudgetExceeded error type (non-retryable by default) and provides an explicit method to force-retry with user confirmation/override.
acceptance_criteria: SDK Python/TS/Go ship helpers that enforce retry budget by default and can be disabled via client config
Server-side contract documented for interpreting X-RW-Id-Key and resume offsets; compatibility tests added to model-hosting infra
Integration test matrix covering: resumable success, resume after transient failure, duplicate suppression when server lacks resume, and budget exhaustion behavior
Telemetry emitted in prod-like environment and visible in Console dashboards for one pilot tenant
Migration doc and examples published (docs.redwood.ai link) and sample code snippets added to SDK repos
implementation_steps: API contract: finalize header/field names and semantics with runtime and gateway teams (contrib: @runtime-team)
Server stubs: runtime implement header parsing and resume/dedupe policy, add test fixtures for resume support and TTL enforcement
SDK primitives: implement RetryBudget helper and IdKeyManager in python-sdk, ts-sdk, go-sdk with identical surface but idiomatic patterns
Backoff telemetry: wire SDKs to emit budget and attempt metrics and add Console ingestion mapping
Docs & samples: write migration guide and code examples; include a 'force retry' knob example and recommended best-practices for long-running streaming jobs
E2E tests: add flaky-network simulation tests in CI that assert no amplification and correct resume behavior
Rollout: staged release: beta flag -> opt-in default for pilot customers -> global default after 4 weeks of telemetry validation
examples: Python: with client.retry_budget.scope(operation_key) as s: streaming = client.stream_upload(file, id_key=s.id_key); streaming.send_chunks() -- helper takes care of budget tokens and id key renewal
TypeScript: const uploader = new RW.UploadStream({retryBudget}); await uploader.pushFile(stream, {idKey}); // uses async iterator wrapper that resumes on retry
Go: sb := sdk.NewBudget("uploads", 5, time.Minute); stream := client.NewChunker(ctx, sb, idKey) // chunker retries transparently up to budget

Server contract example: if X-RW-Resume-Support: true and X-RW-Stream-Offset provided, attempt resume from offset; otherwise, check dedupe table for id key and return 409/duplicate if already observed within TTL
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (beta) - feature flag enabled in SDKs and Console for pilot tenants; manual opt-in via client config
Phase 2 (pilot) - enable for selected customers (identified via ticketing) and monitor retry budget metrics and duplicate rates
Phase 3 (default on) - enable default budgets in SDKs with server-side compatibility checks; keep override flags for 90 days
Phase 4 - refine presets based on telemetry and provide Console recommendations per-tenant
qa_plan: Unit tests for RetryBudget token accounting and edge behaviors (concurrent acquisition, refill race conditions)
Integration tests against runtime mock to exercise resume + dedupe paths
Chaos-tests: simulate transient network failures and verify budget prevents retry amplification
Load-run: synthetic load against a staging tenant to confirm no per-tenant surge when retries occur
Manual review: SDK ergonomics reviewed by developer experience PM and design lead
risks_mitigation: Risk: new headers may not be honored by older runtime nodes — Mitigation: server falls back to dedupe-only behaviour and SDKs expose opt-out
Risk: incorrect id key generation causes accidental deduplication — Mitigation: provide stable id key generator util and migration checklist
Risk: retry budget too small causes higher client-visible failures — Mitigation: conservative defaults (5 tokens/min) and ability to tune per-route
Risk: telemetry spam if too high resolution — Mitigation: sample metrics and aggregate at 10s buckets by default
